Born in England about 1620. He was sheriff at New Haven in 1644, one of the committee that founded Wallingford in
1670, and its deputy to the General Court.
In King Philip's War his house at Wallingford was fortified as a refuge.
He married second, in 1663, Abigail Moss, and died at Wallingford on 11 August 1690.
Baptized at New Haven 10 April 1642, daughter of John Moss, who lived to 103.
Married Sergeant Abraham Doolittle 2 July 1663 as his second wife and went with him to found Wallingford,
where their house was fortified as a picket fort in King Philip's War.
Mother of seven, the youngest Theophilus (1678) .
Widowed in 1690; died at Wallingford 5 November 1710, aged 68.
